title: Strongly inert-active matching and the operadic base filtration
statement:
Use simplicial sets and nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and finite pointed maps, active maps and inert maps of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. Fix $m\geq2$ and put $B_+=N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$ and $B=N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$. Write $\langle s\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,s\}$. A base arrow is strongly inert if its simplex coordinate is constant, its pointed map is inert and the injection of the nonbasepoint fibers is increasing; it is active if its pointed map has preimage of the basepoint equal to the basepoint, and neutral if neither. Every base arrow has a unique factorization as strongly inert followed by active. Call a nondegenerate chain new if its coordinate image contains all $1,\ldots,m$, and closed if its final arity is $1$.
The new nondegenerate chains have the following exhaustive, disjoint matching classification, with an arbitrary prefix permitted wherever one is not specified. Active seeds are closed all-active chains. A shorter neutral chain has a neutral arrow followed by an active block (possibly empty) and then a strongly inert tail (possibly empty). Its unique longer partner replaces that neutral arrow by its strongly-inert/active factorization. Conversely a longer neutral chain has a distinguished strongly inert arrow followed by a nonempty active block and then a strongly inert tail; deleting the intervening factorization vertex, a strictly inner vertex, gives the shorter chain. A shorter output chain is open and consists of an active block followed by a strongly inert tail, either block possibly empty. If its final arity is $s>0$, its longer output partners are exactly the $s$ chains obtained by appending a color projection $\langle s\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$; deleting the last vertex gives the shorter chain. The longer output chains are precisely the closed chains with an active block followed by a nonempty strongly inert tail. A shorter output chain with final arity zero has no partner and is called a nullary seed. Each new chain belongs to exactly one of the active-seed, shorter-neutral, longer-neutral, shorter-output or longer-output classes; the nullary seeds form the indicated subset of the shorter-output class.
For $k\geq0$, let $F_k\subseteq B_+$ be generated by $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\partial\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$, all nondegenerate simplices of dimension $<k$, and the $k$-dimensional longer partners of both kinds. Let $\widehat F_k\subseteq B$ consist of simplices whose strictly positive-coordinate block belongs to $F_k$, allowing an arbitrary initial coordinate-zero block and allowing the positive block to be empty. Then $\widehat F_0=N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Lambda_0^m$, the $\widehat F_k$ increase, and $\bigcup_k\widehat F_k=B$. For $k>0$, $F_k$ is generated over $F_{k-1}$ by active seeds and nullary seeds of dimension $k-1$, and the shorter chains of dimension $k-1$ together with all their longer partners. These assertions remain true after inverse image along any simplicial map $M\to B$, including the arbitrary initial zero blocks. This statement supplies a classification and domains, with no map into a target category and no target extension conclusion.
